papers.title: SpaReg: sparsity-based 3D reconstruction of tissue microenvironments at native resolution across morphological and spatial molecular modalities.
papers.abstract: Tissue microenvironments comprise cellular and acellular components whose three-dimensional (3D) architecture guides disease fate. Direct imaging of intact specimens by lightsheet and multiphoton microscopy, and computational reconstruction from serial sections, have established that 3D spatial context reveals cell and tissue organization inaccessible at single planes. Computational reconstruction in particular can leverage archived human tissue, benefiting from the cost-effectiveness, robustness, scalable storage, workflow compatibility, and century-long pathobiology knowledge of histology, a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: SpaReg is a computational method that reconstructs 3D tissue microenvironments at native resolution from serial tissue sections, integrating both morphological (histology) and spatial molecular data. It leverages sparsity-based approaches to align and reconstruct archived human tissue, enabling 3D spatial analysis without specialized 3D imaging hardware. This makes large-scale 3D spatial studies feasible using existing histology workflows and biobanked specimens.

papers.title: Genomic correlates of metastatic competence and progression in human melanoma.
papers.abstract: Genomic events and their timing that grant a primary tumour the competence to disseminate remain poorly defined. We performed sequencing of 247 stage I/II primary cutaneous melanomas (CMs) and 60 matched metastases without intervening therapy from a prospectively followed registry cohort with a median followup of 92 months, integrating copy-number, mutational, protein and spatial-transcriptomic analyses. Relapse was not distinguished by oncogenic point mutations, which were largely shared between primaries and metastases, but by somatic copy-number alterations (SCNAs) and global chromosomal in
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study sequenced 247 primary cutaneous melanomas and 60 matched metastases to identify genomic events that enable primary tumors to spread. Relapse was not distinguished by oncogenic point mutations, which were largely shared between primaries and metastases, but rather by somatic copy-number alterations and global chromosomal instability. The findings suggest that chromosomal instability, not specific driver mutations, is a key determinant of metastatic competence in melanoma.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA Sequencing Analysis Reveals That Targeting PLG-PLGRKT Signaling-mediated Pro-fibrotic Scar-associated Macrophages Ameliorates Liver Fibrosis in Biliary Atresia.
papers.abstract: Biliary atresia (BA) is a severe pediatric cholangiopathy characterized by rapidly progressive liver fibrosis. This study aimed to characterize scar-associated macrophages and investigate the role of plasminogen (PLG)-plasminogen receptor with a C-terminal lysine (PLGRKT) signaling in BA-associated fibrogenesis.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical and translational hepatology
papers.summary: Using single-cell RNA sequencing, this study characterizes scar-associated macrophages in biliary atresia and identifies PLG-PLGRKT signaling as a driver of their pro-fibrotic activity. Targeting this signaling pathway ameliorated liver fibrosis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for BA-associated fibrogenesis.

papers.title: Macrophage-derived IL-27 sustains autoreactive CD8 + cytotoxic T cells in autoimmune hepatitis.
papers.abstract: Chronic or persistent T cell activation is widely thought to culminate in T cell exhaustion, yet how autoreactive CD8⁺ T cells remain functionally intact despite sustained self-antigen exposure is poorly understood. In chronic infection and cancer this durability is attributed to stem-like, TCF1⁺ PD-1⁺ progenitor-exhausted (Tpex) cells that reside in lymphoid tissue and continuously replenish functional effectors; whether such a reservoir operates within a chronically inflamed peripheral organ during sterile autoimmunity is unknown. Here we show that mice lacking the lysosomal nuclease DNase2a
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study investigates how autoreactive CD8+ T cells maintain their function despite chronic self-antigen exposure in autoimmune hepatitis, a setting where T cell exhaustion would typically be expected. The authors identify macrophage-derived IL-27 as a key factor that sustains these cytotoxic T cells, and provide evidence that a stem-like progenitor-exhausted T cell reservoir may operate within a chronically inflamed peripheral organ during sterile autoimmunity.

papers.title: Lossless compression of protein databases for efficient and accurate metagenomic sequence classification with Centrifuger.
papers.abstract: We present a lossless compression algorithm for indexing a protein database while supporting fast taxonomic classification in the method Centrifuger. The algorithm is a new scheme of the previously proposed run-block compression algorithm to reduce the size of the Ferragina-Manzini (FM) index, and it scales better with alphabet size than the original. On the RefSeq prokaryotic and viral protein sequences, Centrifuger reduces the memory footprint by over a third compared to the method Kaiju that builds on a plain FM-index, while having comparable running time. Furthermore, the compressed FM-ind
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Centrifuger introduces a lossless compression algorithm for indexing protein databases that reduces the memory footprint of the FM-index by over a third compared to Kaiju, while maintaining comparable speed for taxonomic classification of metagenomic sequences. The method scales better with alphabet size, making it practical for large reference databases.

papers.title: Fast, flexible analysis of differences in cellular composition with crumblr.
papers.abstract: Changes in cell type composition play an important role in human health and disease. Recent advances in single-cell technology have enabled the measurement of cell type composition at increasing cell lineage resolution across large cohorts of individuals. Yet this raises new challenges for statistical analysis of these compositional data to identify changes in cell type frequency. We introduce crumblr ( DiseaseNeurogenomics.github.io/crumblr ), a scalable statistical method for analyzing count ratio data using precision-weighted linear mixed models incorporating random effects for complex stud
papers.summary: The authors introduce crumblr, a scalable statistical method for analyzing cell type composition changes in single-cell data. It uses precision-weighted linear mixed models with random effects to handle complex study designs and count ratio data. This enables robust identification of cell type frequency differences across large cohorts.

papers.title: Variation in enhancer activity across brain regions defines neurological disease risk and shapes cellular pathology.
papers.abstract: Genetic variants associated with neurological traits are enriched in enhancers active in neurons. However, there are many types of neurons with varying functions across the brain, making it difficult to pinpoint insights into disease pathology. We set out to investigate whether cell type and brain region specificity of transcriptional enhancers could reveal new insights into the cellular pathology of neurological traits.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how enhancer activity varies across different brain regions and neuronal cell types, aiming to link this variation to neurological disease risk. The authors propose that region- and cell-type-specific enhancers can reveal new insights into the cellular pathology of neurological traits.

papers.title: STAT3D as a new image-tailored Xenium-based spatial transcriptomics tool for accurately dissecting the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables researchers to study gene expression within tumor microenvironments at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue architecture. However, analyzing spatial omics data is challenging due to the complexity of the outputs, including large-scale images, millions of transcripts, and numerous spatial coordinates. Moreover, standard volumetric segmentation is often hampered by optical blurring and signal bleed-through in out-of-focus z-planes, which built-in tools in current platforms (e.g. Xenium Explorer) cannot solve. To overcome these challenges, we introduce ST
papers.summary: The authors present STAT3D, a new computational tool tailored for Xenium spatial transcriptomics data that improves 3D cell segmentation by addressing optical blurring and signal bleed-through in out-of-focus z-planes. This enables more accurate dissection of the tumor microenvironment at single-cell resolution while preserving tissue architecture.

papers.title: Gravlax: an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq.
papers.abstract: A cell-by-gene count matrix is the artifact of a single-cell RNA-seq experiment that is most often stored, shared, and reanalyzed. It is the output of a computation whose inputs are the sequenced molecules and a gene annotation, and while the molecules never change, the annotation is revised continually. Once the matrix has been produced, the evidence behind it can no longer be reinterpreted. Recovering that evidence means returning to raw reads or alignments that are large, costly to process, and frequently unavailable. We ask whether a concise representation of the molecules themselves can b
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Gravlax introduces an annotation-independent molecular evidence archive for single-cell RNA-seq that captures the underlying sequenced molecules rather than the derived count matrix. This allows the molecular evidence to be reinterpreted as gene annotations are continually revised, without needing to reprocess large raw reads or alignments. The approach addresses the loss of re-interpretability inherent in storing only cell-by-gene count matrices.

papers.title: A Real-Data-Driven Framework for Evaluating Differential Transcript Usage Methods Across Long-Read Bulk, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Differential transcript usage (DTU) analysis reveals transcript-level regulation in alternative splicing. With the rapid adoption of long-read sequencing in bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics, reliable evaluation of DTU methods under real biological conditions becomes essential. Current evaluation frameworks mainly rely on simulated data, which can introduce bias and may not reflect true regulatory mechanisms. A real-data-driven framework is constructed to evaluate DTU methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. The framework includes two key components
papers.summary: This paper presents a real-data-driven framework for benchmarking differential transcript usage (DTU) methods across long-read bulk, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomics. Unlike existing frameworks that rely on simulated data, it uses real biological data to evaluate DTU tools, aiming to reduce bias and better reflect true regulatory mechanisms. The framework provides a more realistic assessment of DTU method performance across diverse long-read sequencing applications.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to 1-nitropyrene, a diesel exhaust pollutant, causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice, with extravillous trophoblasts identified as the key affected cell type. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with the Scissor machine learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint core regulatory targets driving trophoblast dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses a genetic multiplexing strategy combined with single-cell RNA-seq to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain across the day-night cycle. It reveals cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics, confirming and extending prior findings about molecular subtypes of these neurons. The work provides a more detailed map of how distinct circadian neuron subtypes regulate gene expression in response to time of day and light.

papers.title: The misplaced mouse Pax6 interneuron subclass: A cross-species transcriptomic reassignment.
papers.abstract: Subclass cell types are strongly conserved across mammalian brains, making the systemic absence of a caudal ganglionic eminence (CGE) Pax6 interneuron subclass in mouse transcriptional atlases unexpected. Through cross-species transcriptomic analysis, we identify a Pax6 subclass homolog in mouse and uncover primate-specific divergence in the Sncg subclass. Analyses of electrophysiological and spatial datasets reveal limited subclass-specific structure in either modality, emphasizing the superior resolving power of transcriptomics for subclass distinctions. Our results highlight the pitfalls of
papers.summary: This study uses cross-species transcriptomic comparisons to identify a mouse homolog of a Pax6 interneuron subclass previously thought absent from mouse brain atlases, and reveals primate-specific divergence in the Sncg subclass. The authors also show that electrophysiological and spatial data have limited power to resolve interneuron subclasses compared to transcriptomics, cautioning against over-reliance on non-transcriptomic modalities for cell-type classification.

papers.title: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics identifies SERPINE1 as a vascular endothelial mediator of cisplatin resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin resistance remains a major obstacle in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), yet the contribution of the vascular microenvironment and its variation across HPV statuses remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell spatial transcriptomics to map the tumor microenvironment in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma and identify vascular endothelial cells as key contributors to cisplatin resistance. The authors pinpoint SERPINE1 as a mediator of this resistance, with potential variation across HPV statuses. The finding suggests targeting the vascular niche, particularly SERPINE1, could help overcome chemotherapy resistance in HNSCC.

papers.title: Cell-resolved spatial mapping of antibody-drug conjugate targets in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) activity and target-dependent on-target/off-tumor toxicity depends in part on which cells express the target antigen, a feature that bulk assays cannot resolve.
papers.summary: This paper uses spatial mapping at single-cell resolution to determine which cells in breast cancer express the antigens targeted by antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). Because ADC efficacy and off-tumor toxicity depend on exactly which cells carry the target, bulk assays miss this critical detail. The approach provides a more precise picture of target expression that could inform ADC design and patient selection.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. They then profiled the gene expression of these cells, which are heavily parasitized and hemophagocytic, to understand their role in parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Spatial Atlas of Small Cell Lung Carcinoma Reveals Intratumoral Tumor-State Heterogeneity and an MMP12+ Macrophage Niche.
papers.abstract: Small-cell lung carcinoma (SCLC) is a highly aggressive tumor with a dismal prognosis among lung cancers. Treatment is failing because of primary or rapidly developing secondary resistance. Recent molecular studies have suggested four SCLC subtypes with unique therapeutic vulnerabilities-ASCL1, NEUROD1, POU2F3, and YAP. These subtypes still distinguish themselves by considerable intra-tumoral heterogeneity and the influence of the microenvironmental context, which are both considered to be responsible for treatment resistance. We integrated in situ hybridization-based spatial transcriptomics w
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to map small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC), revealing that tumors contain heterogeneous mixtures of the four known molecular subtypes rather than a single dominant subtype. The authors also identify a distinct MMP12+ macrophage niche within the tumor microenvironment, suggesting that both intratumoral tumor-state diversity and specific immune cell interactions contribute to treatment resistance.

papers.title: A renal cyst-clear cell renal cell carcinoma comorbidity analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial COL6A1-CD44 axis that remodels fibroblasts.
papers.abstract: Renal cystic conditions are heterogeneous. We used a broad renal cyst-associated disease-gene framework to identify molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), without modeling a specific cystic disorder or direct cyst-to-cancer progression.
papers.summary: This study uses a disease-gene framework for renal cystic conditions to find molecular programs shared with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), rather than modeling a specific cyst-to-cancer progression. The analysis identifies a FOXM1-positive epithelial axis involving COL6A1 and CD44 that appears to remodel fibroblasts in the tumor microenvironment. The findings suggest a potential comorbidity-linked signaling mechanism between cystic kidney disease and ccRCC.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to develop a compact risk score for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma, centered on the HERC5 gene. The authors characterize an immune-attenuated program associated with this risk signature, linking HERC5 to metastatic progression. The work provides a potential transcriptomic biomarker and highlights immune evasion mechanisms in osteosarcoma relapse.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics uncovers an invasive-desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and profound spatial heterogeneity, yet the multicellular organizational principles governing its tumor microenvironment remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq; n = 9) and spatial transcriptomics (n = 4), integrating 61,234 single cells and 30,430 spots to identify an invasive-frontier myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast (IF-myCAF), which is characterized by elevated expression of ACTA2, TAGLN, COL11A1, THBS2, CTHRC1, and POSTN. IF-myCAFs were validated i
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular organization of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, identifying a distinct myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblast population (IF-myCAF) at the invasive frontier. These IF-myCAFs, marked by genes like ACTA2, COL11A1, and POSTN, form a desmoplastic cellular community with prognostic and therapeutic implications.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics elucidates trajectories associated with transformation in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors.
papers.abstract: Tumor invasion and malignant transformation are spatiotemporally coordinated processes that shape clinical behavior, diagnostic classification, and treatment response. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) are aggressive tumors that can arise sporadically or in people with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF-1) yet how distinct spatial niches underlie MPNST intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion or malignant transformation from benign precursors are not fully understood.
papers.summary: This study applies spatial transcriptomics to malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNSTs) to map how distinct spatial niches within tumors drive intra-tumor heterogeneity, local invasion, and malignant transformation from benign precursor lesions. By resolving gene expression trajectories in their spatial context, the work links tumor architecture to the process of malignant progression in NF1-associated and sporadic MPNSTs.

papers.title: Histone H4K5 lactylation-driven feedback loop modulates glycerol-linked immunosuppressive activity of tumor-associated T regulatory cells.
papers.abstract: Tumor metastasis is the leading cause of death for more than 90% of cancer patients, with colorectal cancer (CRC) mainly spreading to the liver. The colon and liver possess distinct nutritional microenvironments, yet how these differences shape the tumor immune landscape remains unclear. Using single-cell analysis of autologous samples from CRC patients with liver metastases, we identified a distinct CD177+GK+ regulatory T (Treg) cell subset in metastatic lesions. Spatial transcriptomics revealed that these GK+ Tregs localize at the tumor-adjacent interface and interact with immunosuppressive
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct CD177+GK+ regulatory T cell subset enriched in colorectal cancer liver metastases, where glycerol kinase (GK) links to an immunosuppressive phenotype. The authors show that histone H4K5 lactylation drives a feedback loop modulating this glycerol-linked immunosuppressive activity of tumor-associated Tregs, revealing a metabolic-epigenetic mechanism shaping the metastatic immune landscape.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: NoiBic is a new biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise when identifying coherent gene expression modules from high-throughput transcriptomic data. It aims to recover meaningful biclusters that would otherwise be obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery in large-scale datasets.

papers.title: Mapping the Tissue Architecture and Endothelial-PEC Network in HAML Using Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) is a rare variant of perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasms (PEComas). Unlike its more common renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), the unique spatial microenvironment of HAML and its specific progression mechanisms remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing and spatial transcriptomics from three sporadic HAML cases. We mapped functionally heterogeneous PEComas subpopulations and their localized tissue niches. Transcriptomic alignment and spatial colocalization demonstrated a high similarity between endothelial cells and a subset of PEC
papers.summary: This study combines single-nucleus RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics across three sporadic hepatic angiomyolipoma (HAML) cases to map the tumor's tissue architecture. The authors identify functionally heterogeneous PEComa subpopulations and their spatial niches, revealing a close transcriptomic and spatial relationship between endothelial cells and a subset of perivascular epithelioid cells (PECs). This provides the first spatially resolved characterization of the HAML microenvironment, distinguishing it from the more common renal angiomyolipoma.

papers.title: SND1 promotes colorectal cancer progression and metastasis by stabilizing HK2 through the inhibition of FBW7-mediated ubiquitination.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, particularly enhanced aerobic glycolysis, is a hallmark of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis. However, the key regulatory mechanisms linking glycolytic remodeling to metastatic progression remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study identifies SND1 as a driver of colorectal cancer progression and metastasis by binding and stabilizing the glycolytic enzyme HK2, shielding it from FBW7-mediated ubiquitination and degradation. This SND1-HK2 axis enhances aerobic glycolysis, providing a mechanistic link between metabolic reprogramming and metastatic progression, and suggests potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP introduces a topic-modeling approach to recover gene-expression programs (GEPs) from single-cell RNA-seq data without forcing each gene into a single program. This better reflects the many-to-many nature of gene regulation, where cells run multiple programs simultaneously and genes participate in several. The method offers a more faithful decomposition of single-cell expression into co-regulated modules.

papers.title: Serval: a modular framework for decoding imaging based spatial transcriptomics data.
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics technologies have opened new avenues for studying cellular organization and gene expression within intact tissues. However, the accuracy of downstream analyses depends critically on the decoding step that reconstructs barcodes from fluorescence patterns and maps them to gene identities. Despite a growing number of decoding methods, systematic benchmarking has been limited.
papers.summary: Serval is a modular framework designed to standardize and benchmark the decoding step in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics, where fluorescence barcode patterns are translated into gene identities. It addresses the lack of systematic benchmarking across the growing number of decoding methods, enabling more reliable downstream analyses of cellular organization and gene expression in intact tissues.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify cell adhesion-related gene signatures associated with cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors use Seurat-based single-cell analysis alongside bulk transcriptomics to characterize how these genes contribute to inflammation and blood-brain barrier disruption, aiming to nominate new therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing with machine learning to dissect the ovarian cancer microenvironment, identifying chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF) subsets as key drivers of poor outcomes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight fibroblast heterogeneity as a clinically relevant factor in residual disease and suggest these subsets as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial biology approaches, particularly spatial transcriptomics, are being applied to cancer epigenetics to study how epigenetic regulation varies across tissue architecture. It argues that disrupting spatial context in bulk and single-cell methods limits understanding of tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions, and highlights opportunities to map epigenetic programs in situ.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide-based bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue structure and protein markers, allowing immunohistochemical analysis of pigmented eye tissues in mice. Using this method, they created a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye, tracking markers like Rpe65, Rhodopsin, and Dct across development, and integrated published single-cell RNA-seq data.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms across three cancer single-cell RNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score (BDS) to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, finding that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that computational pipeline decisions can substantially alter downstream biological conclusions in cancer scRNA-seq studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This paper investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, exploring whether gut microbiota and their metabolites migrate to and influence intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify key microbial species and molecular mechanisms mediating this cross-kingdom communication, though the abstract only states the research gap without presenting results.

papers.title: Integrated scRNA-Seq and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal CHPF and GPC1 as Markers of Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Dominant Domains in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in the colorectal cancer (CRC) tumor microenvironment (TME) is closely related to stromal organization and may influence treatment-related features. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data from CRC tissues to examine cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains. GPC1 and CHPF were enriched in stromal regions and showed higher expression in CRC tissues than in normal tissues. In the analyzed cohorts, higher GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival ou
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to map cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains in colorectal cancer. The authors identify GPC1 and CHPF as markers enriched in stromal regions, with elevated expression in tumor versus normal tissue and association with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival. These findings highlight potential stromal biomarkers linked to tumor microenvironment organization and prognosis.

papers.title: Epithelial to mesenchymal transition and M2 macrophages drive aggressiveness in murine and human sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Patients with majority variant subtype histology including sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma (SUC) have poor outcomes and limited treatment options, and there are few preclinical resources to investigate rare histologic subtypes. We developed three novel variant subtype histology bladder cancer (BC) cell lines by finding that basal BC tumor cells derived from mice treated with N-butyl-N-(4-hydroxybutyl)-nitrosamine (BBN) were initially not competent to grow in immune competent mice, but then acquired tumorigenicity following passaging ("recycling") in mice lacking mature B and T cells. Three ge
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors developed three new mouse-derived bladder cancer cell lines representing sarcomatoid urothelial carcinoma (SUC), a rare and aggressive variant subtype with poor patient outcomes. By passaging basal tumor cells in immunodeficient mice, they generated tumorigenic lines and identified epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and M2 macrophage infiltration as key drivers of SUC aggressiveness in both murine and human tumors.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomics As Rasterized Image Tensors (STARIT) characterizes cell states with subcellular molecular heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatially resolved transcriptomics (imSRT) technologies provide high-throughput molecular-resolution spatial characterization of genes within cells. Conventional analysis methods to identify cell-types and states in imSRT data rely on gene count matrices derived from tallying the number of mRNA molecules detected for each gene per segmented cell, thereby overlooking subcellular heterogeneity that can be useful in defining cell states. To take advantage of the molecular-resolution information in imSRT data and potentially identify cell-states based on subcellular heterogeneity, we
papers.summary: The authors introduce STARIT, a method that treats imaging-based spatial transcriptomics data as rasterized image tensors rather than conventional gene count matrices, preserving subcellular molecular heterogeneity. This allows cell states to be characterized using spatial patterns of mRNA molecules within cells, potentially revealing distinctions that per-cell count matrices miss.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study investigates the relationship between FDX1, a key regulator of mitochondrial metabolism and cuproptosis, and CALR abundance in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs). The authors find that FDX1 expression is associated with CALR levels and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling, suggesting a metabolic-inflammatory link in MPN pathogenesis. The work highlights FDX1 as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target in MPNs.

papers.title: Integrative oxidative stress-disulfidptosis analysis identifies NPR3 and ZNF366 as cell-type-associated candidate markers in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Disulfidptosis is a regulated cell-death program that occurs in SLC7A11-high cells under glucose limitation, but its relationship with oxidative stress in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remains unclear. We integrated 313 oxidative stress-related genes with 24 disulfidptosis-related genes in the original TCGA-KIRC analysis. Pearson screening (|r| ≥ 0.8 and nominal two-sided P < 0.05) identified 21 disulfidptosis-oxidative stress (DOS) genes, from which three reported DOS subtypes, 63 subtype-associated genes and a four-gene score comprising ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3 and NPR3 were derived. In
papers.summary: This study integrates oxidative stress and disulfidptosis gene sets in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) using TCGA-KIRC data, identifying 21 overlapping genes and defining three molecular subtypes. A four-gene prognostic score (ZNF366, EMCN, GRIK3, NPR3) was derived, with NPR3 and ZNF366 highlighted as cell-type-associated candidate markers. The work suggests links between disulfidptosis, oxidative stress, and ccRCC heterogeneity.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates publicly available fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify lipidomic features associated with a colorectal cancer-like metabolic state in precancerous adenomas. The authors propose a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The work is computational and hypothesis-generating, relying on existing public data rather than new experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a pattern of adaptive immune suppression that distinguishes severe acute pancreatitis from milder forms. The findings suggest blood-based transcriptomic signatures could help stratify patients at risk of persistent organ failure.

papers.title: scLTF: A self-training clustering framework for large-scale single-cell RNA-Seq data.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology has rapidly advanced in recent years, driving significant breakthroughs in developmental biology, cancer research, immunology, and other related fields. However, existing clustering methods still face performance bottlenecks when handling large-scale scRNA-seq data. To address this challenge, we propose a self-training clustering method for large-scale single-cell RNA-seq data, termed scLTF (Single-cell Louvain-Transformer Framework for Large-scale Clustering). This method first generates preliminary clusters using a fast Louvain algorithm and
papers.summary: scLTF is a self-training clustering framework designed to handle large-scale scRNA-seq datasets by combining a fast Louvain algorithm for initial clustering with a Transformer-based refinement step. The approach aims to overcome performance bottlenecks of existing clustering methods when applied to very large single-cell datasets.

papers.title: Mitochondrial metabolic plasticity in cancer: hybrid bioenergetic states and translational targeting in surgical oncology.
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial metabolism is increasingly recognized as an active determinant of tumor growth and cancer-cell adaptation rather than solely a source of cellular energy. Mitochondrial metabolism supports tumor anabolism, while mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) alterations can affect respiratory chain function, redox homeostasis, and adaptation to changing tumor environments. At the same time, tumor metabolism is heterogeneous and flexible and cannot be explained by a uniform Warburg model. Tumor cells may use glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), or hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS states, with the re
papers.summary: This review argues that mitochondrial metabolism actively drives tumor growth and adaptation rather than merely supplying energy, with mtDNA alterations influencing respiratory chain function and redox balance. It highlights that tumors display heterogeneous, flexible bioenergetic states—including hybrid glycolysis/OXPHOS phenotypes—that defy a uniform Warburg model, and discusses implications for translational targeting in surgical oncology.

papers.title: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and vasculogenic mimicry in tumor vascular plasticity: a comparative bibliometric analysis and mechanistic framework.
papers.abstract: Endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM) are distinct forms of cellular and vascular plasticity that may contribute to tumor vascular adaptation. Although they have largely evolved as separate research fields, emerging experimental observations suggest potential convergence in their regulation by the tumor microenvironment.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis compares the research landscapes of endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and vasculogenic mimicry (VM), two mechanisms of tumor vascular plasticity that have historically been studied as separate fields. The authors propose a mechanistic framework suggesting these processes may converge under regulation by the tumor microenvironment, highlighting potential crosstalk that could inform future anti-angiogenic strategies.

papers.title: Targeting TREM2+ and TIMD4+ Macrophages Reprograms the Tumor Microenvironment and Enhances PD-1 Blockade Efficacy in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Background: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is the second most common primary liver cancer. Macrophages are crucial components of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2-positive (TREM2+) macrophages have recently emerged as potent pro-tumor progress players in several cancers. However, the heterogeneity and tumor-promoting mechanisms of macrophages especially TREM2+ macrophages in ICC remain systematically unexplored. Therefore, this study aimed to systematically elucidate the heterogeneity of macrophages in ICC, with a specific focus on the pr
papers.summary: This study systematically characterizes macrophage heterogeneity in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC), identifying TREM2+ and TIMD4+ macrophage populations as key pro-tumor players in the tumor microenvironment. Targeting these macrophage subsets reprogrammed the TME and improved the efficacy of PD-1 blockade, suggesting a combination immunotherapy strategy for ICC.

papers.title: Applications of single-cell transcriptomics in glaucoma research: from the aqueous humor outflow pathway to retinal ganglion cell neurodegeneration.
papers.abstract: Glaucoma is the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, driven by progressive retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration. While genetic and environmental risk factors have been identified, the cell-type-specific mechanisms underlying pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution analysis of cellular heterogeneity, developmental trajectories and intercellular communication networks. This review synthesizes recent scRNA-seq advances across two critical domains in glaucoma research: (1) aqueous humor outflow pathway (AHOP) phy
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent single-cell RNA sequencing studies in glaucoma research, focusing on two key areas: the aqueous humor outflow pathway and retinal ganglion cell neurodegeneration. It highlights how scRNA-seq reveals cell-type-specific mechanisms, cellular heterogeneity, and intercellular communication that were previously obscured by bulk approaches.

papers.title: Altered resting-state brain function in diabetic retinopathy: a meta-analysis of combined transcriptome-neuroimaging study.
papers.abstract: Patients with diabetes may develop cognitive dysfunction, particularly at advanced stages of the disease, manifested by impairments in learning, memory, language, and judgment. Previous studies have reported abnormal brain functional alterations in patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR), which may be associated with cognitive impairment in diabetes; however, the molecular correlates of these brain alterations remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis combines resting-state neuroimaging findings with transcriptome data to identify molecular correlates of altered brain function in diabetic retinopathy patients. The authors link specific patterns of brain functional abnormalities to gene expression profiles, suggesting potential mechanisms underlying diabetes-associated cognitive impairment.

papers.title: Decoding the spatial logic of immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: from single-cell profiling to spatial omics.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma remains difficult to treat because immune resistance is organized not only by malignant cell states but also by the spatial architecture of the tumor microenvironment. Single-cell RNA sequencing has clarified cellular heterogeneity in liver cancer, yet tissue dissociation removes the positional relationships that determine whether immune cells can reach and eliminate tumor nests. Spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, and multiplex imaging technologies now make it possible to map immune exclusion, stromal barriers, vascular gatekeeping, tertiary lymphoid structures, macrop
papers.summary: This review argues that immune evasion in hepatocellular carcinoma is driven not just by malignant cell states but by the spatial organization of the tumor microenvironment, which single-cell RNA sequencing alone cannot capture because tissue dissociation destroys positional information. It surveys how spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, and multiplex imaging can map features like immune exclusion, stromal barriers, vascular gatekeeping, and tertiary lymphoid structures to reveal the spatial logic of immune resistance.

papers.title: Structure-based virtual screening identifies ethyl rosmarinate as a SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: SLC1A6 remains poorly characterized in bladder cancer. This study investigated its expression pattern, clinical relevance, cellular localization, functional implications, and potential pharmacological modulation.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the poorly understood glutamate transporter SLC1A6 in bladder cancer, examining its expression, clinical relevance, and cellular function. Using structure-based virtual screening, the authors identify ethyl rosmarinate as a potential SLC1A6-targeted therapeutic candidate for bladder cancer.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omic analysis characterizes an IFNγ-responsive-to-myeloid-suppressive immune continuum in immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is commonly treated as a single inflamed phenotype, although its internal immune heterogeneity remains incompletely defined. We integrated public bulk transcriptomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, proteomic, phosphoproteomic, and treatment-cohort data to test whether this heterogeneity is better represented by discrete states or a continuous immune axis. In 112 checkpoint-high TCGA-LIHC tumors, an inflamed-minus-myeloid axis showed structured heterogeneity but no robust empirical bimodality: the observed kernel-density curve had one prominent
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics, and phosphoproteomics to examine immune heterogeneity in immune-active hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors find that rather than discrete immune states, these tumors lie along a continuous axis ranging from IFNγ-responsive to myeloid-suppressive, with no robust evidence of bimodality. This continuum framework may better capture the internal immune heterogeneity relevant to treatment stratification.

papers.title: Spatial organization of HPV-associated immune programs across tissue compartments in oropharyngeal cancer.
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive oropharyngeal cancer (OPC) is characterized by a distinct immune microenvironment; however, the biological significance of immune-related transcriptional programs may vary according to their spatial localization. We investigated the spatial organization of HPV-associated transcriptional programs across anatomically distinct tissue compartments in OPC.
papers.summary: This study examines how immune-related gene expression programs in HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer are organized across different spatial regions of the tumor tissue. The authors investigate whether the biological meaning of these immune transcriptional signatures depends on where in the tissue they occur, highlighting the importance of spatial context in understanding the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: AI-guided ethnopharmacology for cardiovascular drug discovery: from biomedical data to experimental validation.
papers.abstract: Despite substantial advances in pharmacological therapy, cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Botanical drugs represent a rich source of structurally diverse bioactive metabolites, yet their translation into modern cardiovascular therapeutics remains limited by chemical complexity, incomplete mechanistic understanding, and challenges in experimental validation. Meanwhile, the rapid expansion of biomedical data resources and advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities to systematically investigate botanical drugs beyond empirical a
papers.summary: This review discusses how AI can be integrated with ethnopharmacology to accelerate the discovery of cardiovascular drugs from botanical sources. It outlines a workflow from mining biomedical data through AI-driven prediction to experimental validation, addressing challenges like chemical complexity and incomplete mechanistic understanding of plant-derived compounds.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Reveals Inflammatory Microenvironment and Glycolysis-Driven Epithelial Proliferation in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
papers.abstract: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is a prevalent condition and a leading cause of urinary dysfunction in middle-aged and elderly men. The hyperplasia of prostate stromal and epithelial cells enlarges the prostate, compressing the bladder outlet and resulting in obstructive symptoms. However, the crosstalk between the inflammatory microenvironment and metabolic alterations in BPH remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing to characterize benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), revealing that an inflammatory microenvironment is coupled with glycolysis-driven epithelial proliferation. The findings suggest a crosstalk between immune cell infiltration and metabolic reprogramming in driving prostate enlargement, offering potential mechanistic insight into BPH pathology.
